messages:
Carla: Quick summary — ran an apples-to-apples comparison between synthetic traffic and the replay harness focused on autoscale cold starts + KV-cache warmup. Observed a repeatable p95 spike when scale-up completes and the kernel selector flips. Anyone seen this pattern?

Ben: Which model / sequence length and are you using the new kernel_selector heuristic or the legacy toggle?

Carla: gptx-32k-v1, seq=1024 on A100p. We were on kernel_selector=v2 (experimental). Synthetic bench didn't show the spike; only the replay (real trace) does.

Alice: Putting the short numbers I have: replay p95 ~ 420ms at t=scale-up, baseline synthetic p95 ~ 180ms. CPU->GPU transfer wait spikes in the traces.

dev-bot: replay-harness: run started (id=r-2026-04-21-0912) — injecting traces with original ordering and client-side think times.

Emily: Sounds like KV warmup overlap with kernel swap. When new workers come up they fetch KV cold and the kernel_selector chooses a different matmul path for the first batches. That combo can cause a momentary backpressure.

Frank: Can you paste the small profiler dump? A few lines of nvprof/trace are enough.

Alice: Sure — excerpt: ```
[profile] t=0912.34 gpu_exec_ms=3.4 kernel="cutlass_gemm" batch_size=8
[profile] t=0912.88 gpu_exec_ms=9.6 kernel="fused_attention" batch_size=1
[kv] cache_miss_rate=0.62 prefix_hits=0.38
[serving] dispatch_delay_ms=120 scale_action="add_worker" workers_active=5
```

Carla: The important bit is the dispatch_delay_ms bump right when workers join. That lines up with the p95 blip. We think it's a serialization point in bootstrapping KV for new kernels.

Ben: Did you confirm it's not just cold filesystem reads for weights? Put a md5 check on weight files before/after warmup.

Alice: weights are already cached in tmpfs on our repro pool. md5s identical. This looks more like KV (prefix) misses + kernel handshake.

Emily: For apples-to-apples you also need identical concurrency and ordering. Replay preserves inter-arrival jitters; synthetic tends to flatten them. That might hide races.

Frank: Quick mitigation to validate: 1) force kernel_selector=v1 (old stable) 2) pre-warm KV by replaying top-20 prefixes 3) run on a dedicated pool with burst credits disabled (so we don't get eviction). Command we used: ```
./replay --trace r-2026-04-21.trace --seed-order --prewarm=top20 --kernel-selector=v1 --pool=dedicated-smoke
```

Carla: Good idea. I ran that with prewarm and kernel_selector=v1 — spike disappears (p95 down to ~190ms).

Ben: We should make sure the kernel swap itself is atomic-safe. If kv prewarm reduces miss_rate below ~0.15 then the handshake cost won't coincide with traffic.

Emily: Another angle: change batching heuristic to absorb the first few requests (slightly higher max_latency_ms) so they batch together during warmup and avoid slow-path one-offs. Try bumping batch_window_ms from 5 -> 15 for warmup phase.

Alice: Ran that too — small improvement but not as clean as prewarm. Suggest both: prewarm + temporary batch window increase during scale events.

Frank: Also check burst credits — if worker is started from a burst slot it may be CPU-limited initially. Running on a reserved dedicated pool removed that variable.

Carla: Action items: 1) add a reproducible test in the replay harness that toggles kernel_selector and measures p95 at scale-up (Frank) 2) add a prewarm stage to Dedicated pool spin-up flow (Emily) 3) add a microprofiler check to detect kernel change events and log latency deltas (Alice) 4) follow-up doc describing apples-to-apples checklist (Ben).

Ben: For the doc, checklist minimal: same seed, same ordering, identical think-times, same pool type (dedicated vs shared), same kernel selector flag, same prewarm config. Keep it short.

Carla: I'll run one last end-to-end: replay with kernel=v2 + prewarm + batch_window=15 on dedicated pool and post full traces. If that still shows anomalies we'll record a timed postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:

dev-bot: replay-harness: run completed (id=r-2026-04-21-0912) — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-replay/r-2026-04-21-0912/

Emily: Nice. If this reproduces cleanly we can add an automated check to the autoscale rollout gate.

Frank: Heads-up — I hit a small perf regression in kernel_selector=v2 on kernel memcopy path last week; I can PR a fix and smoke it against the harness tomorrow.

Carla: Perfect — let's sync tomorrow after Frank's patch. Thanks everyone.
